subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Two competing theories of disease transmission dominated medical thought for centuries.
• The Italian physician Girolamo Fracastoro (1478–1553) championed the contagion theory.
• This theory proposed that diseases spread through direct contact between people or contaminated objects.
• The German physician Max von Pettenkofer (1818–1901) supported the miasma theory.
• This theory held that diseases spread through 'bad air' arising from decomposing organic matter.
• In the 1870s, German physician Robert Koch (1843–1910) largely resolved the debate with his experiments demonstrating the role of specific microorganisms in disease.
prompt: The student wants to provide a historical overview of the two theories. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Through two competing theories of disease transmission—contagion and miasma—Fracastoro, Pettenkofer, and Koch held that diseases spread either through direct contact or through contaminated air.
choices.B: While Robert Koch largely resolved the debate in the 1870s, Pettenkofer supported the miasma theory decades before.
choices.C: Medical professionals were divided between the contagion and miasma theories of disease transmission until Robert Koch's 1870s experiments largely resolved the debate in favor of contagion.
choices.D: Before the 1870s, the German physician Max von Pettenkofer supported the miasma theory, which held that diseases spread through 'bad air' arising from decomposing organic matter.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. The sentence provides a historical overview of the two theories, noting that medical professionals were divided between them before Robert Koch's experiments largely resolved the debate in favor of contagion in the 1870s.
